title: Initial Build Offer · Conquistadors ↔ All Hail King Jesus

analysis.executiveSummary: To acquire reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba (99.1 C-AVI / 99.6 D-AVI) from All Hail King Jesus, Conquistadors can offer a balanced package centered on WR George Pickens (92.8 C-AVI), a high-end 2027 1st Round Pick (Northside Kings orig5, 79.3 AVI), and RB Tyjae Spears (50.5 C-AVI). In a 16-team league, All Hail King Jesus has a severe weakness at running back (starting 31-year-old Aaron Jones and Zach Charbonnet) while locking up two elite WRs in JSN and Amon-Ra St. Brown. This proposal gives them a young WR1 replacement in Pickens, immediate RB depth in Spears, and a premium 2027 1st round pick to reload or acquire a star RB, while creating the undisputed #1 WR pairing in the league for Conquistadors (Puka Nacua + JSN) to push for the championship.

submitted.summary: Conquistadors trade concentrated value (Pickens + 2027 1st + Spears) to secure an elite, top-tier asset in Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Upgrading WR2 from George Pickens (92.8 C-AVI) to JSN (99.1 C-AVI) pairs with Puka Nacua (99.6 C-AVI), Josh Allen (99.6 C-AVI), and Bijan Robinson (99.4 C-AVI) to form an unrivaled championship core. All Hail King Jesus gains essential roster depth, a starter-caliber WR, and liquid future draft capital to solve their starting RB crisis.

recommended.summary: This proposal gives All Hail King Jesus a compelling multi-piece return for JSN without destroying their competitive viability, while delivering Conquistadors the highest ceiling starting lineup in the league.

overall.summary: Acquires an S-tier cornerstone wide receiver that elevates the starting lineup ceiling to maximum championship levels.

visualImpact.explanation: This transaction represents a classic 16-team win-now consolidation move for Conquistadors and a roster-rebalancing move for All Hail King Jesus. Conquistadors pay a fair premium (Pickens + 2027 1st + Spears) to secure a rare S-tier wide receiver, while All Hail King Jesus replenishes future capital and backfield depth.

officialAviAnalysis.sideAChampionshipImpact: Upgrades Conquistadors' WR2 position from George Pickens (92.8 C-AVI) to Jaxon Smith-Njigba (99.1 C-AVI). Total starting lineup C-AVI sum increases from 725.3 to 731.6, establishing the most dominant offensive starting 8 in the league.
officialAviAnalysis.sideADynastyImpact: Gains a 24-year-old elite dynasty receiver with a near-perfect 99.6 D-AVI score. Conquistadors retain their own 2028 1st round pick for future flexibility.
officialAviAnalysis.sideARosterImpact: Reduces bench RB depth by sending Tyjae Spears, requiring Conquistadors to monitor waiver/depth running backs behind Bijan Robinson and De'Von Achane.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBChampionshipImpact: Slight immediate hit at WR1 (99.1 JSN to 92.8 Pickens), but provides starting RB flexibility with Spears (50.5 C-AVI) where All Hail King Jesus currently lacks depth.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBDynastyImpact: Acquires George Pickens (96.1 D-AVI, age 25) and a premium 2027 1st round pick (79.3 D-AVI), extending their competitive runway.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBRosterImpact: Helps solve a major structural defect on All Hail King Jesus's roster by converting WR surplus into RB depth and draft liquidity.
officialAviAnalysis.valueAssessment: Total C-AVI sent by Conquistadors is 222.6 for 99.1 received. The 123.5 raw AVI difference represents the exact consolidation premium required to pry an OPOY award-winning 24-year-old dynasty WR1 away from a contending partner in a 16-team league.

publicMarketAnalysis.summary: Public dynasty sentiment places Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the highest tier of untouchable dynasty wide receivers alongside Ja'Marr Chase and Puka Nacua, following his 1,793-yard OPOY season in 2025 and new $168.6M extension.
publicMarketAnalysis.aviVsMarket: AVI rates JSN at 99.1 C-AVI / 99.6 D-AVI, fully aligned with public consensus treating him as an elite multi-year WR1 asset. Market demand requires a young proven WR1/2 plus high 1st-round capital to initiate trade discussions.
relevantContext: JSN signed a 4-year, $168.6M extension with $120M guaranteed, locking him in Seattle through 2031.
Averaged a 32.6% target share and 44.6% first-read share in 2025.
All Hail King Jesus is severely thin at RB in a 16-team format (Aaron Jones, Zach Charbonnet, Isiah Pacheco), making draft capital and RB assets highly attractive to them.

frontOfficeAnalysis.opposingGmMotivation: All Hail King Jesus faces an acute RB depth crisis in a 16-team starting league. Adding a young WR1 (Pickens), an RB piece (Spears), and a 2027 1st round pick gives them the assets needed to retool their backfield while staying highly competitive.
frontOfficeAnalysis.packageFit: Combines a young proven wide receiver (Pickens), an upside RB (Spears), and top-tier future draft capital (2027 1st round pick orig5).
frontOfficeAnalysis.lineupReplacement: Pickens steps directly into All Hail King Jesus's WR starting slot alongside Amon-Ra St. Brown and Tee Higgins, minimizing starting WR drop-off.
frontOfficeAnalysis.competitiveWindowFit: Both franchises remain in strong win-now/contender windows; the trade allows All Hail King Jesus to diversify assets while Conquistadors maximize peak ceiling.
frontOfficeAnalysis.positionalScarcity: In a 16-team league, true 20+ PPG wide receivers are ultra-scarce. Paying a 3-for-1 package is the standard market cost for an S-tier cornerstone.

marketReality.explanation: Though JSN is not explicitly listed on the trade block, All Hail King Jesus's urgent need for running back help and draft capital makes this package a compelling, realistic offer that solves roster imbalance without forcing a complete rebuild.

verdict.rationale: For Conquistadors, acquiring Jaxon Smith-Njigba creates a starting lineup with four 99+ C-AVI players (Josh Allen, Bijan Robinson, Puka Nacua, JSN). Upgrading WR2 from Pickens to JSN significantly elevates weekly championship ceiling while keeping the core intact. The cost (Pickens + 2027 1st + Spears) is substantial but completely justified for your stated goal to Win Championship.

recommendedOffer.whyUserShouldDoIt: It pairs JSN with Puka Nacua to give you the top wide receiver duo in the league, bringing your starting lineup to four 99+ C-AVI megastars for your championship run.
recommendedOffer.whyOpponentMightAccept: It gives All Hail King Jesus a proven 25-year-old WR1 replacement in George Pickens, immediate RB rotation help in Tyjae Spears to fix their weakest position, and a 2027 1st round pick for long-term flexibility.

alternateOffer.rationale: If All Hail King Jesus prefers pure draft capital over Tyjae Spears, substituting Spears with the 2027 2nd Round Pick (Northside Kings orig5) maintains strong package value while keeping Spears on your bench.

analysis.executiveSummary: Shopping De'Von Achane (RB, C-AVI: 97.4) places an elite, weekly slate-breaking RB1 on the trade block. As a championship-focused contender anchored by Josh Allen, Bijan Robinson, and Puka Nacua, trading Achane requires receiving a verified starting-caliber cornerstone in return to maintain title-winning C-AVI lineup scoring. Market analysis identified 3 realistic opportunities with rival contenders where Achane solves critical RB roster bottlenecks, allowing Conquistadors to convert RB surplus into top-tier WR firepower or high-upside starter packages while preserving championship probability.

strengths: Elite QB anchor with Josh Allen (C-AVI: 99.6 / D-AVI: 93.3)
Unmatched RB duo with Bijan Robinson (C-AVI: 99.4) and De'Von Achane (C-AVI: 97.4)
Tier-1 WR centerpiece in Puka Nacua (C-AVI: 99.6 / D-AVI: 99.4)
priorityNeeds: Upgrade WR2/Flex position to match S-tier scoring across all starting spots
Acquire high-upside starting depth to hedge against playoff injury volatility
tradeableSurplus: De'Von Achane (S-Tier RB, peak market liquidity)
constraintsApplied: Goal: Win Championship — strictly maintain or increase starting lineup C-AVI
Starter-for-Starter Realism — Achane must yield a verified starting centerpiece (C-AVI 80+)

eliminationReasons: Rebuilding teams lacked championship-caliber starter assets to package for an elite 24-year-old RB
Rival managers with balanced rosters lacked the specific RB urgency required to give up WR1 cornerstones
Teams unwilling to part with starting lineup pieces were filtered out under Starter-for-Starter rules

opportunities.strategicGoal: Create an untouchable WR tandem (Nacua + London) while acquiring starting RB flex depth.
opportunities.whyUserShouldDoIt: You acquire Drake London (C-AVI: 97.8), a true elite WR1 who locks in alongside Puka Nacua to form the highest-scoring WR core in the league. You also secure J.K. Dobbins in his new high-octane Broncos role as reliable RB depth behind Bijan Robinson.
opportunities.whyOpponentMightAccept: Mile High Royal Lions have Jahmyr Gibbs as their only top-tier RB, with Dobbins as a major liability at RB2. Adding Achane creates the most dominant Gibbs/Achane RB pairing in Autobots history, solving their single biggest title bottleneck while getting a 2027 2nd round pick.
opportunities.championshipImpact: Increases WR/Flex baseline ceiling significantly without sacrificing RB viability.
opportunities.dynastyImpact: Secures two ultra-young 25-and-under cornerstones (London and Nacua) for 5+ years.
opportunities.rosterImpact: Drake London immediately slots into WR2; Dobbins becomes premium RB3 rotational depth.
opportunities.publicMarketContext: London is locked into a $141M extension in Atlanta with a huge target baseline; Achane is entering a expanded volume role in Miami post-shoulder recovery.
risks: Slight reduction in RB tier depth if J.K. Dobbins incurs health setbacks in Denver

negotiationPlan.openingApproach: Offer De'Von Achane straight up for Drake London, emphasizing Achane's elite RB5 PPG ceiling that pairs with Gibbs.
negotiationPlan.acceptableConcession: Include the 2027 2nd round pick (Northside Kings original) and ask for J.K. Dobbins to balance RB depth.
negotiationPlan.walkAwayPoint: Walk away if Mile High Royal Lions require additional 1st round draft capital or Ladd McConkey.

opportunities.championshipImpact: Maintains RB1 scoring tier with Walker in Kansas City while drastically boosting WR flex depth.
opportunities.dynastyImpact: Acquires two young blue-chip starting pieces (ages 25 and 23) in premium offensive systems.
opportunities.rosterImpact: Kenneth Walker slides directly into the starting RB2 slot; Brian Thomas elevates WR flex competition.
opportunities.publicMarketContext: Walker's move to Kansas City has rocketed his redraft/dynasty value; Thomas is widely rated as a premier post-hype bounce-back target in camp.

negotiationPlan.openingApproach: Propose Achane for Walker + Brian Thomas Jr., citing Achane's overall RB1 ceiling in Miami's scheme.
negotiationPlan.acceptableConcession: Add a late 2027 3rd/4th round pick swap if Banditos request minor sweetener.
negotiationPlan.walkAwayPoint: Walk away if Banditos remove Brian Thomas or demand 1st round draft capital.

opportunities.strategicGoal: Upgrade WR flex firepower to Rashee Rice while maintaining explosive RB2 scoring with Omarion Hampton.
opportunities.whyUserShouldDoIt: You acquire Rashee Rice (C-AVI: 96.0), Patrick Mahomes' dominant top target, providing a massive upgrade over Ladd McConkey. You cushion the loss of Achane by securing breakout Chargers starter Omarion Hampton (C-AVI: 91.9) under Mike McDaniel.

opportunities.championshipImpact: Nets a net positive C-AVI gain in starting lineup by upgrading Flex from McConkey (81.9) to Rice (96.0).
opportunities.dynastyImpact: Gains two elite young assets on top-tier passing/running offenses (Chiefs and Chargers).
opportunities.rosterImpact: Hampton takes over starting RB2; Rashee Rice instantly anchors WR2/Flex alongside Puka Nacua.
opportunities.publicMarketContext: Hampton is surging into top-12 RB redraft rankings in McDaniel's offense; Rashee Rice is fully cleared after off-field issues and dominating camp 11-on-11 drills.
risks: Giving up McConkey's long-term Herbert chemistry if Chargers passing volume expands

negotiationPlan.openingApproach: Offer Achane + McConkey for Hampton + Rice, highlighting Achane's S-tier status and McConkey's WR2 youth.
negotiationPlan.acceptableConcession: Include 2027 3rd round pick if Big Balder Brand requests a slight draft bridge.
negotiationPlan.walkAwayPoint: Walk away if Big Balder Brand tries to substitute Rice with Chris Godwin or demands 1st round draft capital.

analysis.executiveSummary: The proposed trade sends elite 24-year-old RB De'Von Achane to Corgi Loaf Baking Co. in exchange for D'Andre Swift, Wan'Dale Robinson, and a 2027 1st-round pick (projected mid-range). While the raw numeric AVI sum of the incoming package appears higher, this deal violates core package realism principles by trading an S-tier cornerstone for secondary depth pieces ('3 dimes for a dollar'). Crucially, for a team committed to winning the championship, downgrading from Achane (97.4 C-AVI) to Swift (76.7 C-AVI) at starting RB2 significantly lowers weekly lineup points and damages championship odds.

officialAviAnalysis.sideAChampionshipImpact: De'Von Achane is a premier fantasy engine (97.4 C-AVI, 292.0 projected PPR points). Moving him deprives Conquistadors of an elite starting RB2 alongside Bijan Robinson, severely weakening weekly championship projection.
officialAviAnalysis.sideADynastyImpact: Achane is a 24-year-old cornerstone RB (96.8 D-AVI) locked into a multi-year high-volume role on a top NFL offense following his lucrative extension.
officialAviAnalysis.sideARosterImpact: Losing Achane leaves Conquistadors with extremely thin RB depth behind Bijan Robinson, forcing Tyjae Spears (50.4 C-AVI) or Keaton Mitchell into prominent roles if Swift suffers any dropoff.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBChampionshipImpact: D'Andre Swift (76.7 C-AVI) provides respectable RB2 production, Wan'Dale Robinson (65.7 C-AVI) adds high-floor WR depth, and the 2027 1st adds zero current points toward the 2026 title.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBDynastyImpact: Swift (86.1 D-AVI, age 27) and Robinson (83.6 D-AVI, age 25) are dependable starter/flex assets, while the 2027 1st (79.3 D-AVI) offers solid long-term draft capital.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBRosterImpact: Corgi Loaf Baking Co. acquires an elite cornerstone RB1, consolidating roster depth into a high-end starter without sacrificing their WR core.
officialAviAnalysis.valueAssessment: Summed AVI (221.7 for Side B vs 97.4 for Side A) is misleading. Elite cornerstones require near-peer quality in return. Exchanging a 24-year-old S-tier RB for an aging RB2, a bench WR, and a future mid 1st dilutes starting lineup advantage.

publicMarketAnalysis.summary: Public consensus views Achane as an explosive elite RB1 who recently signed a 4-year, $64M extension and is fully healthy for camp. Swift is valued as a solid RB2 entering year two in Chicago's Ben Johnson offense, while Wan'Dale Robinson's stock has risen after signing a $70M deal with Tennessee to be Cam Ward's top underneath target.
publicMarketAnalysis.aviVsMarket: AVI's high rating of Achane matches the market's high-ceiling consensus. Swift and Robinson are valued appropriately as high-floor, limited-ceiling starters.
relevantContext: De'Von Achane signed a 4-year, $64M extension in May 2026 and has been fully cleared for training camp.
D'Andre Swift coming off a 1,000-yard season as the lead back in Chicago.
Wan'Dale Robinson reunited with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee as a heavy target sponge.

frontOfficeAnalysis.opposingGmMotivation: Corgi Loaf Baking Co. would be highly motivated to make this trade, as it allows them to package depth and a future pick to acquire a elite S-tier RB to pair with Justin Jefferson and Malik Nabers.
frontOfficeAnalysis.packageFit: From Corgi Loaf's perspective, this deal fits a contender consolidating assets. For Conquistadors, the fit is poor because it weakens an already thin RB room.
frontOfficeAnalysis.lineupReplacement: Swift replaces Achane in the starting lineup but creates a steep drop of 20.7 C-AVI points and 70.3 projected PPR points at RB2.
frontOfficeAnalysis.competitiveWindowFit: Conquistadors are actively in 'Win Championship' mode. Trading away a 24-year-old elite starter for future pick capital directly conflicts with this competitive window.
frontOfficeAnalysis.positionalScarcity: Young S-tier running backs with elite per-touch explosive capability and secured contract volume are among the rarest assets in fantasy football.

marketReality.explanation: While Corgi Loaf Baking Co. would eagerly accept Achane for depth and a pick, this transaction fails crucial validations for Conquistadors. It trades a premier 24-year-old cornerstone for secondary depth and future capital, harming the user's primary goal to win the championship.

verdict.rationale: Conquistadors should decline this deal. Trading away an elite 24-year-old S-tier RB in De'Von Achane (97.4 C-AVI) for D'Andre Swift, Wan'Dale Robinson, and a 2027 1st violates package realism by diluting cornerstone quality into secondary assets. More importantly, as a contender focused on winning the championship, lowering your starting RB2 projection by over 20 C-AVI points directly weakens your starting lineup.
